metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (pricing.cpp) with a deployable entry point (main()), a Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections or writes detected; the single CGI endpoint performs a read-only flat-file lookup and returns HTML. No user-specific state, no downstream service calls, no message producers.

top_gaps.title: CI/CD Automation
top_gaps.gap: No CI/CD pipelines — deployment is manual scp to server
top_gaps.impact: Blocks safe, repeatable deployments and prevents adoption of modern DevOps practices

top_gaps.title: Integration Testing
top_gaps.gap: No automated tests of any kind exist
top_gaps.impact: Cannot validate correctness during changes; high regression risk

top_gaps.title: Unstructured Data Storage
top_gaps.gap: Pricing rules stored in local flat file with no managed storage
top_gaps.impact: Data is not accessible, versionable, or auditable; single point of failure

top_gaps.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage
top_gaps.gap: K8s manifests cover deployment only; no IaC for networking, monitoring, or entry point
top_gaps.impact: Infrastructure changes are manual and non-reproducible

top_gaps.title: Deployment Strategy
top_gaps.gap: Default rolling update only; no canary or blue/green
top_gaps.impact: No ability to catch regressions before full rollout

findings.title: Managed Compute — containerized but not confirmed on managed platform
findings.description: The application has been containerized (Dockerfile with GCC 12 and httpd:2.4-alpine) with Kubernetes deployment manifests targeting EKS. However, no IaC provisions the EKS cluster or confirms managed compute deployment.
findings.gap: Containerization artifacts exist but no IaC confirms the workload runs on managed compute.
findings.recommendation: Provision the EKS cluster via Terraform or CDK and validate that the containerized workload is deployed on managed compute.

findings.title: Network Security — partial hardening, no network policies
findings.description: Container security context is hardened (runAsNonRoot, drop ALL capabilities). Service is ClusterIP (internal). No Kubernetes NetworkPolicy, VPC IaC, or explicit network segmentation.
findings.gap: No Kubernetes NetworkPolicy restricts ingress/egress. Network segmentation is implicit but not enforced.
findings.recommendation: Add Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress. Define VPC/subnet IaC if managing infrastructure.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no gateway or load balancer
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured. Service is ClusterIP only. ALB Ingress is commented out in service.yaml.
findings.gap: Service has no managed entry point — no gateway, load balancer, or traffic management.
findings.recommendation: Deploy AWS ALB Ingress Controller or API Gateway for managed entry point with throttling and health checks.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — static capacity only
findings.description: Kubernetes deployment uses static replicas: 2 with no HPA or auto-scaling mechanism.
findings.gap: No auto-scaling — all capacity is statically provisioned.
findings.recommendation: Configure Kubernetes HPA with CPU/memory-based scaling policies.

findings.title: High Availability — no multi-AZ configuration
findings.description: Kubernetes deployment has 2 replicas but no topology spread constraints, pod anti-affinity, or multi-AZ configuration.
findings.gap: No AZ configuration found. Pods may co-locate on a single node/AZ.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints or pod anti-affinity to distribute pods across AZs.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code Coverage — partial, deployment layer only
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests cover application deployment (namespace, configmap, deployment, service). No IaC for EKS cluster, VPC, monitoring, or DNS.
findings.gap: Partial IaC — deployment manifests only. No infrastructure provisioning for cluster, networking, monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Define complete infrastructure in Terraform or CDK: EKS cluster, VPC, ALB, CloudWatch alarms, DNS.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Makefile install target uses scp for manual deployment. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.gap: No CI/CD — all deployments are manual.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions, CodePipeline) with build, test, push to ECR, deploy to EKS stages.

findings.title: Programming Languages — legacy C++ with pre-C++11 patterns
findings.description: C++ (pre-C++11) with C-style string functions. AWS SDK exists for C++ but cloud-native tooling is narrower than Python/Java/Go/Node.js.
findings.gap: Legacy C++ with pre-C++11 patterns and limited cloud-native tooling ecosystem.
findings.recommendation: Consider rewriting in a cloud-native language (Go, Python, Node.js) or modernize to C++17/20 with proper HTTP framework.

findings.title: API Versioning Strategy — no versioning
findings.description: No API versioning exists. Endpoint is /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi with no version prefix or headers.
findings.gap: No versioning — breaking changes deployed directly.
findings.recommendation: Introduce URL-path versioning (e.g., /v1/pricing) or version headers.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — local flat file, no managed storage
findings.description: Pricing rules stored as pipe-delimited flat file on local filesystem. No S3, no versioning, no parsing pipeline.
findings.gap: Data on local file systems with no managed storage, versioning, or accessibility.
findings.recommendation: Migrate pricing rules to S3 with versioning. Use AWS AppConfig or S3+Lambda for dynamic configuration.

findings.title: API Authentication — no authentication on endpoints
findings.description: CGI endpoint is completely open. No auth middleware, no API Gateway authorizer, no token validation.
findings.gap: No API authentication — endpoints are open to any caller.
findings.recommendation: Add API authentication via API Gateway authorizer (JWT/OAuth2) or Kubernetes ingress with Cognito.

findings.title: Centralized Identity Integration — no IdP integration
findings.description: No integration with any identity provider. Application has no authentication system.
findings.gap: No external IdP integration.
findings.recommendation: When adding authentication, integrate with centralized IdP (Amazon Cognito, Okta).

findings.title: Compute Hardening and Patching — partial hardening, no automation
findings.description: Container is hardened (non-root, drop caps, Alpine). No automated patching or vulnerability scanning.
findings.gap: No patching automation. No vulnerability scanning configured.
findings.recommendation: Integrate container scanning (ECR, Trivy, Snyk) into CI/CD. Automate periodic image rebuilds.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no security scanning
findings.description: No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning. No CI/CD pipeline exists. Known buffer overflow vulnerabilities undetected.
findings.gap: No security scanning tools configured. Known vulnerabilities go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Include SAST (Semgrep, SonarQube) and container scanning (Trivy) in CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no instrumentation
findings.description: No distributed tracing. No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or trace propagation.
findings.gap: No distributed tracing — request flows cannot be traced.
findings.recommendation: Add OpenTelemetry or X-Ray instrumentation. May require language rewrite for proper library support.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — no SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions, no monitoring alarms, no latency/error-rate tracking.
findings.gap: No SLOs — no formal definition of acceptable service levels.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for availability and latency. Implement CloudWatch alarms.

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics
findings.description: No custom metrics published. No business event tracking.
findings.gap: No custom metrics — only default container-level metrics from Kubernetes.
findings.recommendation: Publish business metrics (lookups per SKU, failures) to CloudWatch.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection and Alerting — no alerting configured
findings.description: No alerting configured. Only Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes provide operational signal.
findings.gap: No alerting — failures detected only via pod restarts.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rates and latency. Integrate with PagerDuty/OpsGenie.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — rolling update only
findings.description: Default Kubernetes rolling update with readiness/liveness probes. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting.
findings.gap: Rolling deployments with health checks but no traffic shifting.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments using Argo Rollouts or AWS App Mesh.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no tests exist
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind. README states correctness validated by spot-checking output.
findings.gap: No integration tests — no automated tests at all. High regression risk.
findings.recommendation: Create integration tests validating CGI endpoint with known SKUs. Use container-based testing.

findings.title: Incident Response Automation — no runbooks
findings.description: No runbooks or incident response automation. Only Kubernetes pod restart on liveness failure.
findings.gap: No runbooks — incident response is entirely ad hoc.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common failures. Automate recovery (e.g., auto-rollback on deployment failure).

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no ownership defined
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS, no dashboards, no alarms with named owners, no team attribution.
findings.gap: No observability ownership — monitoring is nonexistent.
findings.recommendation: Define CODEOWNERS. Create service-level dashboard. Assign alarm ownership.
